The 128 had trouble reading a lot of MFM disks. A friend had a pretty decent CP/M rig back then, and getting things to read on my 128 with 1571 was tricky. Not much ran natively without a lot of fiddling either. Truthfully, going between different brands of CP/M computers often didn't work great either. Much like other early cheaper floppy drives, they were finicky. Never had a chance to try a 1581.

"...his estate discovered nearly 200 5.25-inch floppy disks."

Those 5 1/4 double-sided/double density disks held 360K preformatted. So we're talking about less than 70MBs total here. I guess that would be a lot only if they were text documents. MS Word files were actually bigger than they are now.

Doubtful he was using a WYSIWYG editor. Most CP/M used WordStar, and were green screen units, but it sounds like he had some custom software - probably for script formatting. If someone wrote it for him at the time, then getting something to read the files with all the format information into legible text was probably the issue. There were dozens of 'text editors' like that.
